children: Gold slips as traders as investors weigh inflation risks and the Federal Reserve's monetary policy outlook following last week's rate hike. In early European trading, New York futures are down 0.8% to $4,388 a troy ounce. "Gold remains caught between geopolitical and safe-haven support on one side and restrictive US monetary policy on the other, with the outlook for inflation and the pace of additional Fed hikes likely to remain the key drivers," says Soojin Kim from MUFG. Oil prices are down 2% on Monday on easing concerns over disruptions to Saudi pipeline flows despite attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels. But growing expectations of a global cycle of interest-rate increases are weighing on gold, as higher rates make the precious metal less attractive relative to interest-bearing assets. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
